interactions.summary: Jiang answers why the Aeneid can convert Statius but not Virgil by describing poetry as a vessel of holy fire that Virgil distorted into an imperial weapon.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang lecture with brief student prompt.

interactions.summary: Fred returns to the Turnus scene, and Jiang agrees that the sword-belt moment exposes Virgil’s own wish for mercy leaking through an imperial ending he regretted.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student reading followed by Jiang confirmation.

interactions.summary: The reading resumes with Statius explaining that hearing Christian preachers echo Virgil’s lines drew him into baptism and secret Christian commitment.

claims.claim: Jiang says poets channel a holy fire meant to illuminate readers, but Virgil used free will to turn that vessel into an imperial weapon.
Jiang argues the holy fire still leaks out strongly enough that receptive readers can be drawn to Christianity even through a compromised poem.
Virgil cannot be converted by his own poem because the imperial justification he built into it blinds him to the light it still carries.
Jiang endorses the reading that Virgil regretted the merciless ending of the Aeneid and even wished he had burned the manuscript.
The reading has Statius explicitly say that Christian preachers sounded like Virgil, which is how the poem became a road into baptism for him.

signature_moments.moment: Holy fire leaks out of a weaponized poem anyway, reaching readers the poet himself cannot follow.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the holy fire is so strong that there are things that leak out
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the core metaphysical image Jiang uses to explain literature exceeding authorial corruption.

signature_moments.moment: Virgil is blinded by the very moral compromise that let him turn poetry into empire.
signature_moments.source_phrase: this kind of dissonance blinds the poet
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It fuses political temptation with epistemic blindness in one compact diagnosis.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang’s term for the divine energy poetry is meant to carry transparently, even though an author can bend it toward empire.

chronology_notes.note: This packet is a concentrated June 26 statement of Jiang’s literature model: divine content can exceed and even indict the writer who shaped it.
